body_markdown:
# Introduction

English is spoken with many accents around the world. Indian English has its own familiar expressions, rhythm and pronunciation patterns. Some phrases are widely understood in India, while they may sound less familiar elsewhere. Listen to the situation and context to understand the speaker.

## 1. Expressions you may hear in daily conversation

- **Please do the needful.** — Please take the necessary action.
- **I will get back to you.** — I will contact you again with an answer or update.
- **Kindly check.** — Please check this.
- **Please revert.** — In many Indian workplaces, this means please reply. In international English, “please reply” or “please get back to me” is clearer.
- **I am out of station.** — I am away from my usual city or town. “I am out of town” is more widely used internationally.
- **What is your good name?** — A polite way some speakers ask for your name. “What is your name?” is more common internationally.
- **Today itself.** — Today, without delay.
- **Pass out from college.** — In Indian usage, this can mean graduate. In many other varieties, “pass out” usually means become unconscious, so “graduate from college” is clearer internationally.

## 2. Listen to a workplace conversation

Ask someone to read this dialogue aloud, or use text-to-speech. Listen once without reading.

**Manager:** Have you checked the report?  
**Staff member:** Yes, sir. I have checked it.  
**Manager:** Please do the needful and send me an update today itself.  
**Staff member:** Certainly. I will make the changes and get back to you.  
**Manager:** Thank you. Kindly check the figures once more.  
**Staff member:** Sure. I will verify them before sending the report.

## 3. Check your understanding

1. What does “do the needful” mean in this conversation?
   - A. Take the necessary action
   - B. Cancel the report
   - C. Leave the office
2. When should the update be sent?
   - A. Next week
   - B. Today
   - C. Next month
3. What will the staff member check again?
   - A. The office address
   - B. The figures
   - C. The meeting room
4. What does “get back to you” mean?
   - A. Contact you again
   - B. Go home
   - C. Return a document

## 4. Clear alternatives for wider audiences

| Familiar Indian expression | Widely understood alternative |
|---|---|
| Do the needful | Take the necessary action |
| Please revert | Please reply |
| Out of station | Out of town |
| What is your good name? | What is your name? |
| Today itself | Today / before the end of today |
| Passed out of college | Graduated from college |

## Answer key

1. A — Take the necessary action.
2. B — Today.
3. B — The figures.
4. A — Contact you again.

## 5. Listening task

Ask a partner to read the dialogue again. Write down the expressions you hear and explain each one in simple English. Then practise saying the alternatives in the table.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming every Indian English expression is understood in every country.
- Using “passed out” when you mean graduated in an international conversation.
- Guessing an unfamiliar phrase without considering the situation.

## Learning tip

Accents and expressions vary. Focus on understanding the speaker's meaning, and choose clear, simple phrases when speaking to an international audience.

faq.answer: Listen to the examples, repeat them aloud, complete the exercises and review the answer key.

faq.answer: Start slowly to notice the sound or meaning, then repeat at a natural speaking pace.
